processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Applied to the cast steel blocks (vacuum arc furnace) to promote uniform composition and microstructure; common preparation for all steels S1–S5 including S2.
Homogenized steel subjected to step-by-step hot rolling reducing thickness to ~11 mm, followed by slow cooling in the oven.

Fixed austenitization temperature of 1150 °C applied to S1, S2, S4 and S5 to eliminate αp and dissolve carbides; hold 15 min (S1, S2, S5). Before heat treatment, cylindrical specimens (ø5 x 10 mm³) were fabricated by water jet cutting.

processing_steps.method: continuous cooling from austenitization to austempering temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cooling at 100 K/s is sufficiently fast to suppress intermediate phase transformations and ensure fine bainitic transformation.
TB = 350 °C selected slightly above the measured Ms of 274 °C to obtain nB microstructure. For S2 at 350 °C the bainitic transformation completed in ~2300 s with an incubation time of 210 s.

structures.overall_structure: αp-free nano-bainitic (nB) microstructure: bainitic ferrite laths (nB Type 1 and Type 2/interlocked morphology at 350 °C) with blocky retained austenite (γr) between the sheaves and (Fe,M)xCy carbide precipitates; no polygonal ferrite.

phases_present.morphology: blocky regions located between bainitic sheaves at TB 350 °C
rounded/spherical cementite-like carbides (M = Si, Mo), located near γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries; nucleated (not spinodal)

precipitates.distribution: near γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries; observed by SEM in S2 at 300 °C and 350 °C

defect_interactions.interaction_type: micro-strain / dislocation distribution between γr and bainitic ferrite
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: At TB 350 °C and 300 °C for S2, both bainitic ferrite and γr phases exhibit similar ε values in the range 0.44–0.47 % (εγ 0.45 %, εα 0.44 % at 350 °C), indicating no significant phase-resolved micro-strain difference; (Fe,M)xCy precipitates sit near the γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Bainitic transformation at TB 350 °C yields blocky retained austenite (Vγ = 34 %) and coarser bainitic laths (Lt(t) = 68 nm) than at lower TB; the interlocked nB Type 1/Type 2 plus blocky γr morphology is characteristic of the higher austempering temperature.
interfaces.interface_notes: Carbides observed near the γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries and were only detectable due to localized brightness under SEM.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: ASTM E8 sub-size round specimen: 12.5 mm gauge length, 2.5 mm diameter, 7 mm shoulder length
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile specimens heat-treated using the DIL 805A dilatometer applying the thermal cycle of Fig. 1(a) with the transformation finish time Bt; tested on a Zwick/Roell universal testing machine (250 kN load cell).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss AG, Jena, Germany; samples etched with 6 % Nital solution; ImageJ (v1.53) image analysis
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal microstructural features and verify the presence/absence of polygonal ferrite (αp)
characterization_methods.key_findings: S2 was αp-free at 1050 °C and αp-free at the selected TA of 1150 °C.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: DIL 805A dilatometer (TA Instruments, New Castle, DE, USA)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Heating 10 K/s, cooling 100 K/s; cylindrical specimens ø5 x 10 mm³
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine measured austenitizing temperature TA, martensite start temperature Ms, and bainitic transformation kinetics (Bt)
characterization_methods.key_findings: S2 measured TA = 1031 °C (MatCalc 929 °C, applied 1150 °C); Ms = 274 °C; at TB 350 °C the bainitic transformation completed in ~2300 s with 210 s incubation; at 300 °C Bt = 3600 s with 130 s incubation.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss AG, Jena, Germany; gold sputter-coated etched samples; ImageJ for bainite thickness
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine bainite lamellar thickness and observe precipitate morphology
characterization_methods.key_findings: S2 at 300 °C shows fine lath/needle bainite with (Fe,M)xCy; at 350 °C coarser sheaves/plates with (Fe,M)xCy; (Fe,M)xCy have rounded morphology with no micro-void formation.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: EDX of precipitates in S1, S2 and S3 (Fig. 9 (j))
characterization_methods.key_findings: Confirms (Fe,M)xCy carbides with M = Si, Mo; Si interpreted as entrapped due to rapid cooling, Mo enhances stability; carbon only used to detect (Fe,M)xCy due to EDX limitations.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Malvern Panalytical Empyrean diffractometer, Cu Kα radiation (40 kV/40 mA), PIXcel 1D detector
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine retained austenite volume fraction (Vγ) and phase micro-strains (εγ, εα)

characterization_methods.technique: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) plus SEM imaging
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss SEM with Oxford Instruments EBSD system and software; 20 kV accelerating voltage, step size 0.2 μm
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Surface prepared by grinding, electropolishing and vibratory polishing
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase and grain orientation analysis; support of microstructural interpretation
characterization_methods.key_findings: Used for the microstructural study; MatCalc/XRD considered quantitative for phase fractions.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Equilibrium step calculations and TTP precipitation kinetics
characterization_methods.purpose: Assist austenitizing temperature determination and precipitation/precipitation kinetics prediction
characterization_methods.key_findings: For S2 predicted ferrite-free TA = 929 °C and carbide-dissolution Tcd = 1107 °C; (Fe,M)xCy precipitates between ~700 and 1150 °C during cooling; S1 TTP panel taken as approximately representative for S2.

computational_details.simulation_method: Equilibrium phase (step) calculation and precipitation kinetics / TTP diagram simulation
computational_details.software_used: MatCalc (Version: 6.01 (rel 1.003), Institute of Materials Science and Technology, TU Wien, Wien, Austria)
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Standard step calculation method; thermodynamic system fcc, bcc, liquid, κ-carbide, hcp carbide, AlN, TiCN–TiMoC; classical nucleation theory with dislocation and grain-boundary sites, ortho-equilibrium transformation; volumetric misfit considered; κ-carbide treated as fixed phase fractions
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Heat treatment cycle of the bainitic transformation (austenitization at applied TA, cooling at 100 K/s, isothermal austempering at TB); used to predict ferrite-free TA and carbide-dissolution temperature
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted ferrite-free TA = 929 °C for S2 versus measured TA = 1031 °C and applied TA = 1150 °C; (Fe,M)xCy precipitation predicted above the austempering (bainitic hold) temperature, consistent with SEM observations.

analytical_models.equation_role: Rietveld-based calculation of retained austenite volume fraction from integrated intensities accounting for carbide fraction

unmapped_findings: Product of strength and elongation (PSE) for S2 austempered at 350 °C is 12,970 MPa·% (≈13.0 GPa·%), the peak performance of alloy S2 (Sections 3.3 and 4).
S2 bainitic transformation kinetics at TB 350 °C: incubation time 210 s and bainite finish time Bt ≈ 2300 s; at TB 300 °C: incubation 130 s and Bt = 3600 s.
S2 measured Ms = 274 °C, measured TA = 1031 °C, MatCalc ferrite-free TA = 929 °C, applied TA = 1150 °C (Table 2 / Fig. 4).

S2 (with ~0.1 wt.% higher C than S1) showed only minor mechanical differences from S1: at 300 °C S2 gave UTS ~1590 MPa and El 7.0 % (PSE 11,130 MPa·%) — this belongs to the sibling 300 °C condition, not the 350 °C sample.
Some studies relate Al addition to accelerating bainitic transformation; S1 and S2 behave similarly with higher C shifting bainitic transformation onset toward lower temperatures.
General observation: 8.08 wt.% Al design (S3) is detrimental to ductility at lower TB; C variations near 1 wt.% are secondary to Al level; Ti+Ni alloying in S4 compensates for lower C.
